prerequisites: It is recommended to take the course together with the first-year courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Evaluates the economic aspects of product development.
Knows how to incorporate ergonomic constraints into mechanical design. Performs Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) for the Project.
Applies new technologies in project development and management.
Generates the graphical documentation that allows for the construction of a prototype.

Achieves the intended operation for the designed and built prototype. Develops strategies to obtain results in the appropriate time and with precise scope. Is capable of overcoming difficulties arising from the work, both individually and in a group.

Takes into account the points of view of others and provides constructive feedback. Identifies the collective objectives of the group with their own. Contributes to the establishment and application of team work processes. Through their communication and interaction, contributes to group cohesion.

Participates actively and shares information, knowledge, and experiences. Carries out their individual contribution within the foreseen time and with available resources. Accepts and complies with group rules. Actively collaborates in team work planning, task distribution, and required deadlines.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Course logistics and project descriptions will be discussed. Methods and processes used for product development will also be explained.
Product planning: Some methods and tools for planning development projects.

Identification of customer needs: The concept of customer needs will be reviewed, and practical exercises on identifying needs will be carried out; this aims to prepare students to identify needs in each of the projects that each team will develop.
Product specifications: Technical specifications that respond to customer needs will be established. Different types of specifications and the difficulty in determining some of them will be analyzed.
Concept generation: Generation of concepts that solve our problem. Some methods.
Concept selection: Selection of the concept to be developed by each team. Selection methods.
Concept testing: Verification, comparison of the selected concept.
Industrial design: Areas of industrial design. Fundamentals and development over time.
Design for manufacturing: Robust Design. Design of experiments. Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA).
Prototyping: Need for prototypes. Plans and experiences of prototype creation related to their project.
Project management: Global project review. Feedback.
teaching_methods: Introductory activities: Activities aimed at making contact, gathering student information, and presenting the course.

Preliminary project: This involves carrying out projects that allow the integration of competencies developed in various subjects and that confront students, working in teams, with open problems that make them practice, among others, their capacities for cooperative learning, leadership, organization, communication, and strengthening personal relationships. The result of the preliminary project is a machine that must be submitted to a public test. The correct functioning of the machine is essential to pass the course.
Seminars: Contents will be developed with brief presentations and case analysis. In these sessions, the course contents will be developed.
Presentations/expositions: Public presentation of the developed project and the design decisions adopted and models used in the development of the built machine.

assessment_methods.method: Preliminary project: The result of the preliminary project is a mechanical device that will be submitted to a public competition. The grade will depend on the demonstrated functioning of the machine. Correct functioning is essential to pass the course.

Presentations/expositions: Public presentation of the developed project and the design decisions adopted and models used in the development of the built machine. The evaluation will be carried out by the team of professors.
Mixed tests: Tests related to the ability to apply the different contents of product development. In each of the tests, a minimum grade of 4.0 will be required.
Other: Minimum participation/attendance in laboratory/manufacturing sessions may be considered in the evaluation.

assessment_rules: The preliminary project (40%), presentations (30%), and mixed tests (30%) contribute to the final grade. A minimum grade of 4.0 out of 10 is required in each mixed test. Correct functioning of the machine in the preliminary project is essential to pass the course. The course has only one evaluation call; students cannot request an additional examination call.
bibliography: Karl T. Ulrich y Steven D. Eppinger, Product Design and Development, 2a. Irwin McGraw-Hill, 2000
